rules.title: Check the critical drainage area boundary
rules.text: Use the Torbay CDA criteria for conservative screening across Torbay. For a site in Maidencombe, establish the current EA designation and boundary before relying on CDA status in a formal assessment.
rules.when: All development that could affect drainage.
rules.check: The site against the current designation map, the applicable local policy and any written confirmation of the 2026 extension. Record the boundary and the basis of the assessment.
rules.note: Sources differ. The Local Plan (2015) and SFRA Level 1 (June 2026) say the whole of Torbay is a CDA. The Validation List (November 2024) and the draft SFRA Level 2A (June 2026) say Maidencombe is outside it. The EA national dataset published in September 2026 has a July 2025 geometry revision and does not establish the extension. Whole-Torbay screening is the working interpretation, not confirmation of a new formal boundary. The local Validation List still requires an FRA in Maidencombe.
evidence: Dated designation map and recorded assessment basis
Locate the application boundary and identify the source version. For Maidencombe, record the published source difference and the confirmation relied on.
A general statement that the whole borough is designated, without addressing the boundary evidence.

rules.title: Seek a contribution to wider flood risk reduction
rules.text: Development in the CDA should be served by SuDS meeting the CDA criteria and should also contribute to a scheme that reduces risk for those liable to flood, for example by improving a constrained channel, culvert or bridge.
rules.when: New development in the CDA, proportionate to scale.
rules.check: Whether the proposal identifies or contributes to a downstream improvement. ER1 allows a financial contribution to be requested.
evidence: Site-specific flood risk assessment and dated map extracts; Topographical survey, proposed levels, access drawings and any applicable emergency plan; Flood-zone compatibility, applicable sequential or exception test evidence, and coastal-risk assessment where relevant
Whether the proposal identifies or contributes to a downstream improvement. ER1 allows a financial contribution to be requested.

rules.title: Require a flood risk assessment with a surface water drainage strategy
rules.text: A flood risk assessment (FRA), including a surface water drainage strategy, is a local validation requirement for householder, full, outline and reserved matters applications and relevant demolition in a conservation area.
rules.when: All listed application types anywhere in Torbay. For prior approvals, compare Validation List 4.1.4 and 4.2.15 and record the applicable planning class, submission scope and assessment basis. Their stated scopes differ; seek Council clarification where applicability is uncertain.
rules.check: That an FRA is submitted before validation. Householder development in Flood Zone 1 can normally use the short Torbay proforma.
evidence: Site-specific flood risk assessment and dated map extracts; Topographical survey, proposed levels, access drawings and any applicable emergency plan; Flood-zone compatibility, applicable sequential or exception test evidence, and coastal-risk assessment where relevant
That an FRA is submitted before validation. Householder development in Flood Zone 1 can normally use the short Torbay proforma.

rules.title: Require a site-specific FRA where NPPF F4 applies
rules.text: A site-specific FRA should accompany development proposals in Flood Zones 2, 3a and 3b. In Flood Zone 1, it should inform and accompany proposals on sites of 1 ha or more, land the EA has identified as having critical drainage problems, or land identified in an SFRA or the Flood Map for Planning as being at risk from any source now or in future.
rules.when: Any development meeting an F4 trigger. Confirm the current EA-designated boundary where that trigger is material; local FRA requirements also apply.
rules.check: The F4 trigger and evidence, and an FRA proportionate to the scale, nature and location of the development, covering relevant flood sources, future climate and lifetime.
evidence: Site-specific flood risk assessment
Identify the F4 trigger from the flood zone, site area, EA designation or SFRA/Flood Map evidence. Trace relevant flood sources, future conditions and lifetime through the proportionate assessment.
A single Flood Zone image or an assessment that omits the relevant source or trigger.

rules.title: Check the Local Plan FRA level
rules.text: A basic FRA for all development; a more detailed FRA for Flood Zone 1 sites of 1 ha or more (including those draining into Flood Zones 2 and 3), all new development in Flood Zones 2 and 3, and development near seafronts at risk from wave action.
rules.check: That the depth of the FRA matches the ER1 category.
evidence: Site-specific flood risk assessment and dated map extracts; Topographical survey, proposed levels, access drawings and any applicable emergency plan; Flood-zone compatibility, applicable sequential or exception test evidence, and coastal-risk assessment where relevant
That the depth of the FRA matches the ER1 category.

rules.title: Apply the sequential test
rules.text: Steer development to the lowest flood risk land where suitable alternative sites are reasonably available. Torbay's Validation List includes a flooding sequential test for new dwellings in Flood Zones 2 and 3. Check the current national exemptions and the applicable local requirements.
rules.when: Development at risk now or in future from any source, unless an exemption in NPPF F5.2 is demonstrated.
rules.check: That the sequential test is passed or the precise F5.2 exemption is supported by evidence. The test area should not exceed the anticipated catchment of the development's occupiers or users.
rules.note: F5.2 exempts allocated sites tested during plan preparation; sites where an FRA clearly demonstrates that no built development, access or escape routes, land raising or other vulnerable elements are on land at risk now or in future; or surface-water-only risk where layout, design and mitigation meet F7 lifetime safety without increasing risk elsewhere. It also exempts householder development, non-residential extensions with a footprint less than 250 m², and changes of use other than to caravan, camping, chalet, mobile home or park home sites.
evidence: Sequential-test evidence or precise exemption
Match the proposal and FRA to the relevant F5.2 exemption, or demonstrate the sequential test using suitable reasonably available alternatives and the appropriate catchment.
An obsolete change-of-use exemption or an unsupported assertion that the site is exempt.

rules.title: Check flood-zone compatibility and the exception test
rules.text: Check the use against NPPF Annex F tables 2 and 3: incompatible development should be refused. Where the exception test applies, demonstrate wider sustainability benefits that outweigh flood risk, lifetime safety under F7, and no increase in flood risk elsewhere with an overall reduction where possible.
rules.when: Development in Flood Zones 2, 3a or 3b; the exception-test requirement depends on vulnerability and the exemptions in NPPF F6.2.
rules.check: Flood-zone and vulnerability classification, compatibility, all three exception-test criteria supported by the FRA, or the evidenced F6.2 exemption.
rules.note: F6.2 removes the exception-test requirement for forms or circumstances exempt from the sequential test under F5, and for allocated sites tested at plan-making stage unless flood risk has since significantly increased or the proposal has changed significantly to introduce a more vulnerable use. This does not remove the separate flood-zone compatibility check.
evidence: Flood-zone compatibility and exception-test evidence
Check Annex F classification and compatibility first, then all three F6.1 criteria or the precise F6.2 exception-test exemption.
A passed exception test used to justify an incompatible use, or a missing lifetime-safety or off-site-risk criterion.

rules.title: Make development safe from flooding
rules.text: Development should not present a flood risk to occupiers, users or visitors or increase flood risk elsewhere. Where risk exists now or in future, locate the most vulnerable development in the lowest risk areas unless overriding reasons justify otherwise. Demonstrate lifetime safety for its users, safe management of residual risk and, where appropriate, safe access and escape as part of an agreed emergency plan. Provide flood resistance and resilience allowing rapid return to use without significant refurbishment.
rules.when: All development at risk of flooding now or in future.
rules.check: Siting and any overriding reasons, lifetime safety, finished floor levels, residual risk, the applicable emergency plan and access arrangements, resilience and effects elsewhere.
evidence: Lifetime safety, residual-risk and resilience evidence
Relate the layout, any overriding siting reasons, user vulnerability, applicable emergency plan, access, resilience and effects elsewhere to the assessed present and future flood conditions.
Safe access asserted without the relevant emergency arrangements, or resilience described without an effective return-to-use outcome.

rules.title: Set finished floor levels above the design flood level
rules.text: Set finished floor levels above the 1 in 100 year flood level, with climate change, where the site is at risk.
rules.check: Floor levels against modelled flood levels.
evidence: Site-specific flood risk assessment and dated map extracts; Topographical survey, proposed levels, access drawings and any applicable emergency plan; Flood-zone compatibility, applicable sequential or exception test evidence, and coastal-risk assessment where relevant

rules.title: Coastal change and future tidal inundation
rules.text: NPPF F9 covers coastal change management areas and other areas likely to face coastal erosion or tidal inundation over the next century. Demonstrate lifetime safety, consistency with the relevant Shoreline Management Plan without unacceptable effects on coastal change processes, and wider sustainability benefits that justify development. Torbay's Validation List requires a coastal change vulnerability assessment within a coastal change management area.
rules.when: Sites within a coastal change management area or other areas within the national F9 risk scope.
rules.check: The national coastal-erosion map and current local evidence, all F9 criteria, any applicable local vulnerability-assessment requirement and drainage effects on coastal stability.
evidence: Coastal-risk scope and assessment evidence

rules.title: No basement accommodation where there is danger of inundation
rules.text: Basement accommodation, including changes of use or basement parking, will not be permitted where there is danger of inundation and risk to life.
rules.when: Proposals with basements in areas at risk.
rules.check: Basement flood risk in the FRA.
evidence: Site-specific flood risk assessment and dated map extracts; Topographical survey, proposed levels, access drawings and any applicable emergency plan; Flood-zone compatibility, applicable sequential or exception test evidence, and coastal-risk assessment where relevant

rules.title: Use the 2026 SFRA maps
rules.text: Check the SFRA surface water maps (current and future) and the Flood Zone 3b map, alongside the EA Flood map for planning.
rules.check: That the FRA uses the current SFRA mapping, not superseded 2008 or 2010 data.
evidence: Site-specific flood risk assessment and dated map extracts; Topographical survey, proposed levels, access drawings and any applicable emergency plan; Flood-zone compatibility, applicable sequential or exception test evidence, and coastal-risk assessment where relevant

rules.title: Follow the destination hierarchy
rules.text: Discharge runoff to the following destinations, to the maximum extent practicable, in this order: 1 collect for non-potable use; 2 infiltrate to ground; 3 discharge to an above-ground surface water body; 4 discharge to a surface water sewer or other piped surface water system; 5 discharge to a combined sewer.
rules.check: That each higher destination has been assessed and used as far as practicable.
rules.note: The Local Plan (2015) and the Torbay guide (2022) start the hierarchy at infiltration. The national standards (2025) put reuse first. Reuse first is the current national position in standard 1.2.
evidence: Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights
That each higher destination has been assessed and used as far as practicable.

rules.title: Evidence for using a lower destination
rules.text: Evidence shall show all higher priority destinations have been used to the maximum extent practicable. Higher cost alone is not a reason to use a lower destination.
rules.check: Site evidence (tests, levels, distances), not assertion or cost alone.
evidence: Destination appraisal
For each higher destination, identify the site evidence, practicable use and reason any remaining runoff needs a lower destination.

rules.title: Maximise each destination in order
rules.text: Where more than one destination is used, maximise each one's ability to accept runoff in order of priority.
rules.check: The proportion of area to each destination.
evidence: Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights

rules.title: Contamination is not an automatic reason to move down
rules.text: Do not discount higher priority destinations because a site is or was contaminated where practicable remediation can be designed with the drainage.
rules.check: That remediation and drainage options were considered together.
evidence: Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights
That remediation and drainage options were considered together.

rules.title: Secure rights over third-party land
rules.text: Where discharge needs third-party land, provide evidence of easements for the lifetime of the development.
rules.when: Outfalls or routes across land not owned by the applicant.
rules.check: Easement or agreement evidence. Where rights cannot be obtained, the council may have powers under FWMA 2010 Schedule 2 paragraph 29(1).
evidence: Land-rights evidence and route plan
Match the proposed connection and access route to the land affected and the rights needed for construction, use and maintenance.

rules.title: No increase in flood risk elsewhere
rules.text: Runoff from the development shall not increase flood risk elsewhere from any source.
rules.check: Downstream effects, adjacent land and the receiving system.
evidence: Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights

rules.title: No depletion of waters
rules.text: The design shall not deplete surface waters or groundwater beyond safe environmental levels.
rules.when: Schemes that divert runoff away from its natural catchment or receiving water.
rules.check: That natural catchments are replicated as far as practicable.
evidence: Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights
That natural catchments are replicated as far as practicable.

rules.title: Keep surface water out of foul sewers
rules.text: Essentially uncontaminated surface water shall not discharge to a foul-only sewer. The national standards except runoff integral to a foul pumping station. Very contaminated runoff is dealt with separately under the water quality requirements, including any consent for foul discharge.
rules.check: The runoff type, sewer classification, connection drawings and any consent for the exceptional discharge.
evidence: Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights
The runoff type, sewer classification, connection drawings and any consent for the exceptional discharge.

rules.title: Consider rainwater harvesting
rules.text: Rainwater harvesting shall be considered where there is a non-potable demand with enough catchment, a need for landscape irrigation, or the area is seriously water stressed.
rules.when: Any of the three triggers applies. Examples include industrial, commercial, educational, public sector, residential and multiple-occupancy buildings.
rules.check: A reasoned demand assessment. If harvesting is not used, the reason.
evidence: Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights

rules.title: Design rainwater harvesting for its intended use
rules.text: Harvesting used to manage large rainfall events shall be designed to BS EN 16941. Harvesting design shall follow best practice and demonstrate effectiveness against a rainfall time series. Communal systems outside the curtilage shall consider public health and security.
rules.when: Rainwater harvesting is proposed; apply the large-event and communal-system conditions where relevant.
rules.check: Rainfall time series, demand profile, applicable design standard and public health and security assessment.
evidence: Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights
Rainfall time series, demand profile, applicable design standard and public health and security assessment.

rules.title: Agree discharge to a watercourse in writing
rules.text: The principle of discharge to an above-ground water body, including rates and volumes, shall be agreed in writing with the relevant risk management authority. This does not replace permits or consents.
rules.check: Written agreement in principle; ordinary watercourse consent or EA permit as needed.
evidence: Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights
Written agreement in principle; ordinary watercourse consent or EA permit as needed.

rules.title: Agree sewer connections in writing with capacity
rules.text: Discharge to a surface water sewer, other piped drainage or combined sewer shall be agreed in writing with the relevant risk management authorities and the downstream owner if different. Include rates, volumes, connection location and confirmation of capacity.
rules.check: Written agreements from the relevant authorities and owner; capacity evidence and the proposed connection point.
evidence: Written connection and capacity evidence
Check the receiving system, location, proposed discharge and the agreed capacity basis against the submitted design.
An enquiry acknowledgement or a sewer-location plan used as connection approval.

rules.title: Combined sewer: control to greenfield and assess pollution
rules.text: A combined sewer is the last destination in the hierarchy. ER2 requires greenfield discharge rates. Assess pollution from surcharge or flooding of the receiving combined sewer and provide mitigation demonstrating that pollution risk is not increased. Where capacity is insufficient, the developer should work with the undertaker to fund capacity.
rules.check: Hierarchy evidence, greenfield rate, receiving sewer capacity, pollution assessment and effective mitigation.
evidence: Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights
Hierarchy evidence, greenfield rate, receiving sewer capacity, pollution assessment and effective mitigation.

rules.title: Torquay: appropriate assessment where the hierarchy is not met
rules.text: In Torquay, development that has not met the ER2 drainage hierarchy will be subject to an individual Habitats Regulations Appropriate Assessment.
rules.when: Torquay sites that do not meet the hierarchy.
rules.check: Refer to the council ecologist.

rules.title: Pumping by exception only
rules.text: Pumping shall be by exception and agreed with the approving body. Assess pumping against a lower destination reachable by gravity, including cost, failure risk, pollution and flooding. Pump only the parts that cannot drain by gravity.
rules.check: The gravity alternative, the area pumped and the failure assessment.
evidence: Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights
The gravity alternative, the area pumped and the failure assessment.

rules.title: Pumping station design and downstream capacity
rules.text: Design pumping stations to recognised guidance unless an alternative is agreed in writing with the proposed adoption organisation and the approving body if different. Where a downstream pumping station receives the flow, provide written confirmation of capacity from its owner.
rules.when: Pumped systems or downstream pumping stations.
rules.check: Design standard and owner capacity letter.
evidence: Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights

rules.title: Ask for a fallback destination
rules.text: Ask for a fallback (Plan B) destination if infiltration proves unsuitable at detailed design or a connection is refused.
rules.when: Outline and full applications relying on infiltration or an unconfirmed connection.
rules.check: A deliverable fallback that still meets the discharge limits.
evidence: Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights
A deliverable fallback that still meets the discharge limits.

rules.title: Prove infiltration with site testing
rules.text: Infiltration depends on suitable ground and adequate tested rates. Geotechnical investigation shall confirm the ground is suitable using recognised methods. Mapping can form an initial evidence base.
rules.when: Infiltration proposed, or evidence needed to assess its feasibility. Mapping can inform whether ground investigation is necessary.
rules.check: Adequate site evidence for the hierarchy decision; location-specific investigation and testing where infiltration is relied on.
evidence: Located investigation and test records; Groundwater and geotechnical evidence; Feature sections and infiltration calculations
Adequate site evidence for the hierarchy decision; location-specific investigation and testing where infiltration is relied on.

rules.title: Test to BRE 365 at the feature location and depth
rules.text: Test in strict accordance with BRE 365 at the location and depth of each feature (or within 20 m where results are similar). Three consecutive tests to near emptying; extrapolation from 25% effective depth is not accepted. Permeable paving tested at 20 m intervals with pits at least 1.5 m × 1 m.
rules.check: Test locations against the layout; three fills; full drainage.
evidence: Test plan and test records

rules.title: Keep 1 m above maximum groundwater
rules.text: The base of infiltration features shall be at least 1 m above the maximum likely groundwater level. For systems wholly relying on infiltration this 1 m unsaturated zone also protects groundwater.
rules.check: Base level against groundwater evidence.
evidence: Groundwater evidence and feature section

rules.title: Establish wet-winter groundwater levels
rules.text: Confirm groundwater levels through investigation during high groundwater periods, using records at or near the site, with enough data to show seasonal levels.
rules.check: Monitoring period and season. Single dry-season readings are not enough.
rules.note: There is no Torbay rule for the monitoring period. Devon asks for monitoring over November to May (reference only).
evidence: Located investigation and test records; Groundwater and geotechnical evidence; Feature sections and infiltration calculations
Monitoring period and season. Single dry-season readings are not enough.

rules.title: No unacceptable instability, pollution or groundwater flooding
rules.text: Infiltration shall not cause unacceptable instability or subsidence (including riverbanks and coastal features), groundwater or surface water pollution, groundwater flooding, or ingress to foul or combined sewers.
rules.check: Ground risk assessment. Torbay guide 4.2 lists slopes over 10%, unstable or contaminated ground, services and proximity.
evidence: Located investigation and test records; Groundwater and geotechnical evidence; Feature sections and infiltration calculations
Ground risk assessment. Torbay guide 4.2 lists slopes over 10%, unstable or contaminated ground, services and proximity.

rules.title: Deep-bore infiltration by exception
rules.text: Deep-bore infiltration is not a SuDS approach. It shall be by exception with an agreement in principle from the relevant risk management authority.
rules.check: Exceptional justification and EA agreement or permit.
evidence: Located investigation and test records; Groundwater and geotechnical evidence; Feature sections and infiltration calculations
Exceptional justification and EA agreement or permit.

rules.title: Do not rely only on point infiltration below 1×10⁻⁶ m/s
rules.text: Point infiltration (for example soakaways) shall not be fully relied on where infiltration rates are below 1×10⁻⁶ m/s.
rules.check: Tested rate. If lower, an additional destination.
evidence: Located investigation and test records; Groundwater and geotechnical evidence; Feature sections and infiltration calculations
Tested rate. If lower, an additional destination.

rules.title: Half-empty within 24 hours
rules.text: Infiltration features shall half-empty their runoff volume within 24 hours for events up to the 3.3% AEP event.

evidence: Infiltration storage and half-drain calculation

rules.title: Use the Torbay factor of safety
rules.text: Size infiltration with the RP156 factor of safety. Torbay expects the 'minor damage to external areas or inconvenience' values: 2 for areas under 100 m², 3 for 100 to 1000 m², 5 for over 1000 m². Use 10 where failure would damage buildings or cause major inconvenience.

rules.check: Factor used against drained area and consequence.
evidence: Calculation input and consequence assessment

rules.title: Assess point infiltration within 5 m of structures
rules.text: Where runoff goes to point infiltration within 5 m of existing or proposed buildings, roads, embankments or other infrastructure, assess instability and mitigate. Unstable geology may need more than 5 m.
rules.check: Distances on the layout and the stability assessment.

rules.text: Diffuse near-surface infiltration taking direct rainfall or a very small catchment similar in area to the infiltration surface should not normally pose a structural risk. rules.title: Protect infiltration surfaces from clogging
rules.text: Features that infiltrate should include or be preceded by pre-treatment that protects the infiltration surface.

rules.title: Groundwater protection and contaminated land
rules.text: Follow EA groundwater protection guidance when discharging to ground. Infiltration through contaminated land is allowed only where there is no risk of mobilising pollutants.

rules.text: Where infiltration lies beneath trafficked surfaces, consider structural loading and soil weakening when saturated.

rules.text: Deliver interception within the development so the first 5 mm of rainfall produces no runoff for at least 80% of summer events (May to October) and 50% of winter events (November to April).

rules.text: Optional deemed-compliance route: a development is deemed compliant if rainwater harvesting means no runoff leaves the development for lower-order events, shown by BS EN 16941 calculations. This does not require the feature to be provided.

rules.text: Optional deemed-compliance route: a development is deemed compliant if it infiltrates entirely to ground so no runoff leaves for events with a 1 in 1 or greater chance each month, shown by calculations and infiltration tests. rules.text: Surfaces with green roofs or walls that drain only their own area comply.

rules.text: Provide a management and maintenance plan that sustains performance against standards 1–6 for the development’s lifetime. Torbay asks for the plan and an inspection checklist. The detailed management and maintenance contents in national standards 7.10–7.11 are recommendations.
rules.when: All applicable development; establish the delivery arrangements at outline and supply detail appropriate to the application stage.
rules.check: Responsibilities and funding; asset and land ownership; easements; operating and pollution-incident instructions; establishment and routine maintenance; inspections, sediment and pollution controls and disposal; remedial work, replacement and post-flood rehabilitation.
evidence: Asset-specific management and maintenance plan
Identify each asset, responsible party, lifetime arrangements and practical maintenance. Use the recommended contents in their stated context.
A generic schedule with no asset ownership or delivery arrangements.

rules.title: Consider failure scenarios
rules.text: Examine the likelihood and consequences of operational failure, including blocked structures and controls and failed pumps. Evaluate both flood risk and water quality impacts and manage the risks. The design should make consequential blockage or clogging apparent from surface inspection.
rules.check: Flood-risk and water-quality failure assessment, safe operation and the means of detecting failure.
evidence: Asset-specific maintenance plan and inspection information; Ownership, adoption and usable access arrangements; Construction, phasing, commissioning and structural evidence

rules.title: Access for maintenance
rules.text: Allow free, safe and easy access (with easements) for people, vehicles and machinery, including for emergencies.
rules.check: Access routes on the layout.

rules.title: Sediment removal
rules.text: Design the system so sediment, detritus and debris can be easily removed. Easily emptied, replaced or rehabilitated sediment controls are recommended where deposits could harm performance or design life. Establish the lawful waste classification, handling and disposal route for removed material.
rules.check: Access, sediment controls, removal method, waste classification and the applicable disposal requirements.
evidence: Asset-specific maintenance plan and inspection information; Ownership, adoption and usable access arrangements; Construction, phasing, commissioning and structural evidence

rules.title: Automatic monitoring of pumps and proprietary products
rules.text: Where pumps or proprietary below-ground products (for example separators) are used, provide automatic monitoring and failure warnings to the responsible body.

rules.title: Minimise energy and prioritise source control
rules.text: As far as reasonably practicable, minimise energy use over the design life. Prioritise source control to minimise large downstream attenuation ponds with safety-critical maintenance requirements.
rules.check: Distribution of features; pumping avoided.

rules.title: Construction information and phasing
rules.text: Give the contractor information on protecting and commissioning drainage during construction. For phased developments, provide a phased plan showing flow control in each phase.

evidence: Construction and phasing information

rules.title: CDM and materials
rules.text: Designers take account of construction, operation, maintenance and decommissioning risks under CDM 2015 and minimise them as far as reasonably practicable. Specify materials suitable for their intended use, having regard to preserving natural resources and minimising embedded carbon.
rules.check: Designer’s risk assessment, operational access and suitable material specifications; no invented carbon threshold.

rules.title: Departures
