FR-01.title: Check the critical drainage area boundary
FR-01.text: Use the Torbay CDA criteria for conservative screening across Torbay. For a site in Maidencombe, establish the current EA designation and boundary before relying on CDA status in a formal assessment.
FR-01.when: All development that could affect drainage.
FR-01.check: The site against the current designation map, the applicable local policy and any written confirmation of the 2026 extension. Record the boundary and the basis of the assessment.
FR-01.note: Sources differ. The Local Plan (2015) and SFRA Level 1 (June 2026) say the whole of Torbay is a CDA. The Validation List (November 2024) and the draft SFRA Level 2A (June 2026) say Maidencombe is outside it. The EA national dataset published in September 2026 has a July 2025 geometry revision and does not establish the extension. Whole-Torbay screening is the working interpretation, not confirmation of a new formal boundary. The local Validation List still requires an FRA in Maidencombe.

FR-02.title: Seek a contribution to wider flood risk reduction
FR-02.text: Development in the CDA should be served by SuDS meeting the CDA criteria and should also contribute to a scheme that reduces risk for those liable to flood, for example by improving a constrained channel, culvert or bridge.
FR-02.when: New development in the CDA, proportionate to scale.
FR-02.check: Whether the proposal identifies or contributes to a downstream improvement. ER1 allows a financial contribution to be requested.

FR-03.title: Require a flood risk assessment with a surface water drainage strategy
FR-03.text: A flood risk assessment (FRA), including a surface water drainage strategy, is a local validation requirement for householder, full, outline and reserved matters applications and relevant demolition in a conservation area.
FR-03.when: All listed application types anywhere in Torbay. Prior approvals also need an FRA (Validation List 4.1.4 and 4.2.15).
FR-03.check: That an FRA is submitted before validation. Householder development in Flood Zone 1 can normally use the short Torbay proforma.

FR-04.title: Require a site-specific FRA where NPPF F4 applies
FR-04.text: A site-specific FRA should accompany development proposals in Flood Zones 2, 3a and 3b. In Flood Zone 1, it should inform and accompany proposals on sites of 1 ha or more, land the EA has identified as having critical drainage problems, or land identified in an SFRA or the Flood Map for Planning as being at risk from any source now or in future.
FR-04.when: Any development meeting an F4 trigger. Confirm the current EA-designated boundary where that trigger is material; local FRA requirements also apply.
FR-04.check: The F4 trigger and evidence, and an FRA proportionate to the scale, nature and location of the development, covering relevant flood sources, future climate and lifetime.

FR-05.title: Check the Local Plan FRA level
FR-05.text: A basic FRA for all development; a more detailed FRA for Flood Zone 1 sites of 1 ha or more (including those draining into Flood Zones 2 and 3), all new development in Flood Zones 2 and 3, and development near seafronts at risk from wave action.
FR-05.check: That the depth of the FRA matches the ER1 category.

FR-06.title: Apply the sequential test
FR-06.text: Steer development to the lowest flood risk land where suitable alternative sites are reasonably available. Torbay's Validation List includes a flooding sequential test for new dwellings in Flood Zones 2 and 3. Check the current national exemptions and the applicable local requirements.
FR-06.when: Development at risk now or in future from any source, unless an exemption in NPPF F5.2 is demonstrated.
FR-06.check: That the sequential test is passed or the precise F5.2 exemption is supported by evidence. The test area should not exceed the anticipated catchment of the development's occupiers or users.
FR-06.note: F5.2 exempts allocated sites tested during plan preparation; sites where an FRA clearly demonstrates that no built development, access or escape routes, land raising or other vulnerable elements are on land at risk now or in future; or surface-water-only risk where layout, design and mitigation meet F7 lifetime safety without increasing risk elsewhere. It also exempts householder development, non-residential extensions with a footprint less than 250 m², and changes of use other than to caravan, camping, chalet, mobile home or park home sites.

FR-07.title: Check flood-zone compatibility and the exception test
FR-07.text: Check the use against NPPF Annex F tables 2 and 3: incompatible development should be refused. Where the exception test applies, demonstrate wider sustainability benefits that outweigh flood risk, lifetime safety under F7, and no increase in flood risk elsewhere with an overall reduction where possible.
FR-07.when: Development in Flood Zones 2, 3a or 3b; the exception-test requirement depends on vulnerability and the exemptions in NPPF F6.2.
FR-07.check: Flood-zone and vulnerability classification, compatibility, all three exception-test criteria supported by the FRA, or the evidenced F6.2 exemption.
FR-07.note: F6.2 removes the exception-test requirement for forms or circumstances exempt from the sequential test under F5, and for allocated sites tested at plan-making stage unless flood risk has since significantly increased or the proposal has changed significantly to introduce a more vulnerable use. This does not remove the separate flood-zone compatibility check.

FR-08.title: Make development safe from flooding
FR-08.text: Development should not present a flood risk to occupiers, users or visitors or increase flood risk elsewhere. Where risk exists now or in future, locate the most vulnerable development in the lowest risk areas unless overriding reasons justify otherwise. Demonstrate lifetime safety for its users, safe management of residual risk and, where appropriate, safe access and escape as part of an agreed emergency plan. Provide flood resistance and resilience allowing rapid return to use without significant refurbishment.
FR-08.when: All development at risk of flooding now or in future.
FR-08.check: Siting and any overriding reasons, lifetime safety, finished floor levels, residual risk, the applicable emergency plan and access arrangements, resilience and effects elsewhere.

FR-09.title: Set finished floor levels above the design flood level
FR-09.text: Set finished floor levels above the 1 in 100 year flood level, with climate change, where the site is at risk.
FR-09.check: Floor levels against modelled flood levels.

FR-10.title: Coastal change and future tidal inundation
FR-10.text: NPPF F9 covers coastal change management areas and other areas likely to face coastal erosion or tidal inundation over the next century. Demonstrate lifetime safety, consistency with the relevant Shoreline Management Plan without unacceptable effects on coastal change processes, and wider sustainability benefits that justify development. Torbay's Validation List requires a coastal change vulnerability assessment within a coastal change management area.
FR-10.when: Sites within a coastal change management area or other areas within the national F9 risk scope.
FR-10.check: The national coastal-erosion map and current local evidence, all F9 criteria, any applicable local vulnerability-assessment requirement and drainage effects on coastal stability.

FR-11.title: No basement accommodation where there is danger of inundation
FR-11.text: Basement accommodation, including changes of use or basement parking, will not be permitted where there is danger of inundation and risk to life.
FR-11.when: Proposals with basements in areas at risk.
FR-11.check: Basement flood risk in the FRA.

FR-12.title: Use the 2026 SFRA maps
FR-12.text: Check the SFRA surface water maps (current and future) and the Flood Zone 3b map, alongside the EA Flood map for planning.
FR-12.check: That the FRA uses the current SFRA mapping, not superseded 2008 or 2010 data.

RD-01.title: Follow the destination hierarchy
RD-01.text: Discharge runoff to the following destinations, to the maximum extent practicable, in this order: 1 collect for non-potable use; 2 infiltrate to ground; 3 discharge to an above-ground surface water body; 4 discharge to a surface water sewer or other piped surface water system; 5 discharge to a combined sewer.
RD-01.check: That each higher destination has been assessed and used as far as practicable.
RD-01.note: The Local Plan (2015) and the Torbay guide (2022) start the hierarchy at infiltration. The national standards (2025) put reuse first. Reuse first is the current national position in standard 1.2.

RD-02.title: Evidence for using a lower destination
RD-02.text: Evidence shall show all higher priority destinations have been used to the maximum extent practicable. Higher cost alone is not a reason to use a lower destination.
RD-02.check: Site evidence (tests, levels, distances), not assertion or cost alone.

RD-03.title: Maximise each destination in order
RD-03.text: Where more than one destination is used, maximise each one's ability to accept runoff in order of priority.
RD-03.check: The proportion of area to each destination.

RD-04.title: Contamination is not an automatic reason to move down
RD-04.text: Do not discount higher priority destinations because a site is or was contaminated where practicable remediation can be designed with the drainage.
RD-04.check: That remediation and drainage options were considered together.

RD-05.title: Secure rights over third-party land
RD-05.text: Where discharge needs third-party land, provide evidence of easements for the lifetime of the development.
RD-05.when: Outfalls or routes across land not owned by the applicant.
RD-05.check: Easement or agreement evidence. Where rights cannot be obtained, the council may have powers under FWMA 2010 Schedule 2 paragraph 29(1).

RD-06.title: No increase in flood risk elsewhere
RD-06.text: Runoff from the development shall not increase flood risk elsewhere from any source.
RD-06.check: Downstream effects, adjacent land and the receiving system.

RD-07.title: No depletion of waters
RD-07.text: The design shall not deplete surface waters or groundwater beyond safe environmental levels.
RD-07.when: Schemes that divert runoff away from its natural catchment or receiving water.
RD-07.check: That natural catchments are replicated as far as practicable.

RD-08.title: Keep surface water out of foul sewers
RD-08.text: Essentially uncontaminated surface water shall not discharge to a foul-only sewer. The national standards except runoff integral to a foul pumping station. Very contaminated runoff is dealt with separately under the water quality requirements, including any consent for foul discharge.
RD-08.check: The runoff type, sewer classification, connection drawings and any consent for the exceptional discharge.

RD-09.title: Consider rainwater harvesting
RD-09.text: Rainwater harvesting shall be considered where there is a non-potable demand with enough catchment, a need for landscape irrigation, or the area is seriously water stressed.
RD-09.when: Any of the three triggers applies. Examples include industrial, commercial, educational, public sector, residential and multiple-occupancy buildings.
RD-09.check: A reasoned demand assessment. If harvesting is not used, the reason.

RD-10.title: Design rainwater harvesting for its intended use
RD-10.text: Harvesting used to manage large rainfall events shall be designed to BS EN 16941. Harvesting design shall follow best practice and demonstrate effectiveness against a rainfall time series. Communal systems outside the curtilage shall consider public health and security.
RD-10.when: Rainwater harvesting is proposed; apply the large-event and communal-system conditions where relevant.
RD-10.check: Rainfall time series, demand profile, applicable design standard and public health and security assessment.

RD-11.title: Agree discharge to a watercourse in writing
RD-11.text: The principle of discharge to an above-ground water body, including rates and volumes, shall be agreed in writing with the relevant risk management authority. This does not replace permits or consents.
RD-11.check: Written agreement in principle; ordinary watercourse consent or EA permit as needed.

RD-12.title: Agree sewer connections in writing with capacity
RD-12.text: Discharge to a surface water sewer, other piped drainage or combined sewer shall be agreed in writing with the relevant risk management authorities and the downstream owner if different. Include rates, volumes, connection location and confirmation of capacity.
RD-12.check: Written agreements from the relevant authorities and owner; capacity evidence and the proposed connection point.

RD-13.title: Combined sewer: control to greenfield and assess pollution
RD-13.text: A combined sewer is the last destination in the hierarchy. ER2 requires greenfield discharge rates. Assess pollution from surcharge or flooding of the receiving combined sewer and provide mitigation demonstrating that pollution risk is not increased. Where capacity is insufficient, the developer should work with the undertaker to fund capacity.
RD-13.check: Hierarchy evidence, greenfield rate, receiving sewer capacity, pollution assessment and effective mitigation.

RD-14.title: Torquay: appropriate assessment where the hierarchy is not met
RD-14.text: In Torquay, development that has not met the ER2 drainage hierarchy will be subject to an individual Habitats Regulations Appropriate Assessment.
RD-14.when: Torquay sites that do not meet the hierarchy.

RD-15.title: Pumping by exception only
RD-15.text: Pumping shall be by exception and agreed with the approving body. Assess pumping against a lower destination reachable by gravity, including cost, failure risk, pollution and flooding. Pump only the parts that cannot drain by gravity.
RD-15.check: The gravity alternative, the area pumped and the failure assessment.

RD-16.title: Pumping station design and downstream capacity
RD-16.text: Design pumping stations to recognised guidance unless an alternative is agreed in writing with the proposed adoption organisation and the approving body if different. Where a downstream pumping station receives the flow, provide written confirmation of capacity from its owner.
RD-16.when: Pumped systems or downstream pumping stations.
RD-16.check: Design standard and owner capacity letter.

RD-17.title: Ask for a fallback destination
RD-17.text: Ask for a fallback (Plan B) destination if infiltration proves unsuitable at detailed design or a connection is refused.
RD-17.when: Outline and full applications relying on infiltration or an unconfirmed connection.
RD-17.check: A deliverable fallback that still meets the discharge limits.

IG-01.title: Prove infiltration with site testing
IG-01.text: Infiltration depends on suitable ground and adequate tested rates. Geotechnical investigation shall confirm the ground is suitable using recognised methods. Mapping can form an initial evidence base.
IG-01.when: Infiltration proposed, or evidence needed to assess its feasibility. Mapping can inform whether ground investigation is necessary.
IG-01.check: Adequate site evidence for the hierarchy decision; location-specific investigation and testing where infiltration is relied on.

IG-02.title: Test to BRE 365 at the feature location and depth
IG-02.text: Test in strict accordance with BRE 365 at the location and depth of each feature (or within 20 m where results are similar). Three consecutive tests to near emptying; extrapolation from 25% effective depth is not accepted. Permeable paving tested at 20 m intervals with pits at least 1.5 m × 1 m.
IG-02.check: Test locations against the layout; three fills; full drainage.

IG-03.title: Keep 1 m above maximum groundwater
IG-03.text: The base of infiltration features shall be at least 1 m above the maximum likely groundwater level. For systems wholly relying on infiltration this 1 m unsaturated zone also protects groundwater.

IG-04.title: Establish wet-winter groundwater levels
IG-04.text: Confirm groundwater levels through investigation during high groundwater periods, using records at or near the site, with enough data to show seasonal levels.
IG-04.check: Monitoring period and season. Single dry-season readings are not enough.
IG-04.note: There is no Torbay rule for the monitoring period. Devon asks for monitoring over November to May (reference only).

IG-05.title: No unacceptable instability, pollution or groundwater flooding
IG-05.text: Infiltration shall not cause unacceptable instability or subsidence (including riverbanks and coastal features), groundwater or surface water pollution, groundwater flooding, or ingress to foul or combined sewers.
IG-05.check: Ground risk assessment. Torbay guide 4.2 lists slopes over 10%, unstable or contaminated ground, services and proximity.

IG-06.title: Deep-bore infiltration by exception
IG-06.text: Deep-bore infiltration is not a SuDS approach. It shall be by exception with an agreement in principle from the relevant risk management authority.
IG-06.check: Exceptional justification and EA agreement or permit.

IG-07.title: Do not rely only on point infiltration below 1×10⁻⁶ m/s
IG-07.text: Point infiltration (for example soakaways) shall not be fully relied on where infiltration rates are below 1×10⁻⁶ m/s.
IG-07.check: Tested rate. If lower, an additional destination.

IG-08.title: Half-empty within 24 hours
IG-08.text: Infiltration features shall half-empty their runoff volume within 24 hours for events up to the 3.3% AEP event.

IG-09.title: Use the Torbay factor of safety
IG-09.text: Size infiltration with the RP156 factor of safety. Torbay expects the 'minor damage to external areas or inconvenience' values: 2 for areas under 100 m², 3 for 100 to 1000 m², 5 for over 1000 m². Use 10 where failure would damage buildings or cause major inconvenience.
IG-09.when: Infiltration designed with the RP156 (CIRIA) method.
IG-09.check: Factor used against drained area and consequence.

IG-10.title: Assess point infiltration within 5 m of structures
IG-10.text: Where runoff goes to point infiltration within 5 m of existing or proposed buildings, roads, embankments or other infrastructure, assess instability and mitigate. Unstable geology may need more than 5 m.
IG-10.check: Distances on the layout and the stability assessment.

IG-11.title: Assess diffuse infiltration within 3 m of buildings
IG-11.text: Diffuse near-surface infiltration taking direct rainfall or a very small catchment similar in area to the infiltration surface should not normally pose a structural risk. Such proposals within 3 m of a building shall be assessed and mitigated where required. This reassurance does not extend to large contributing catchments.
IG-11.when: Permeable surfaces or similar within 3 m of a building.
IG-11.check: Distance, contributing area relative to the infiltration surface, ground conditions, structural risk and any mitigation.

IG-12.title: Protect infiltration surfaces from clogging
IG-12.text: Features that infiltrate should include or be preceded by pre-treatment that protects the infiltration surface.
IG-12.check: Silt traps, filter strips or other pre-treatment.

IG-13.title: Groundwater protection and contaminated land
IG-13.text: Follow EA groundwater protection guidance when discharging to ground. Infiltration through contaminated land is allowed only where there is no risk of mobilising pollutants.
IG-13.when: Infiltration, especially on brownfield land or in source protection zones.

IG-14.title: Structural loading below trafficked surfaces
IG-14.text: Where infiltration lies beneath trafficked surfaces, consider structural loading and soil weakening when saturated.

ER-01.title: Intercept the first 5 mm
ER-01.text: Deliver interception within the development so the first 5 mm of rainfall produces no runoff for at least 80% of summer events (May to October) and 50% of winter events (November to April).
ER-01.check: Interception method for every positively drained surface.

ER-02.title: Design interception with quality, amenity and biodiversity
ER-02.text: Show the everyday rainfall approach was developed alongside water quality, amenity and biodiversity.
ER-02.check: That interception features are part of the landscape and treatment train.

ER-03.title: Deemed compliance: harvesting
ER-03.text: A development is deemed compliant if rainwater harvesting means no runoff leaves the development for lower-order events, shown by BS EN 16941 calculations.

ER-04.title: Deemed compliance: full infiltration of monthly events
ER-04.text: A development is deemed compliant if it infiltrates entirely to ground so no runoff leaves for events with a 1 in 1 or greater chance each month, shown by calculations and infiltration tests. A soakaway designed for 1 in 1 or 1 in 10 year events already meets this.

ER-05.title: Simplified approach needs agreement
ER-05.text: Where no modelling is used, the simplified approach (features and ratios in 2.7) may be accepted with the approving body's agreement. Where a feature lacks capacity, downstream features can add it, with detailed calculations.

ER-06.title: Green roofs and walls
ER-06.text: Surfaces with green roofs or walls that drain only their own area comply.
ER-06.check: That no other area drains onto the roof.
ER-06.note: This is a compliance presumption for the proposed feature, not a requirement to provide it. Apply the agreement and calculation conditions in ER-05 and national standards 2.6.2–2.7.

ER-07.title: Rainwater harvesting and water butts
ER-07.text: Surfaces draining to BS EN 16941 harvesting based on regular daily non-potable demand comply. Water butts limited to garden use in dry periods do not.
ER-07.check: Daily demand basis; water butts not counted unless designed with calculations.
ER-07.note: This is a compliance presumption for the proposed feature, not a requirement to provide it. Apply the agreement and calculation conditions in ER-05 and national standards 2.6.2–2.7.

ER-08.title: Permeable surfaces
ER-08.text: No added area: complies (lined or unlined). Unlined with added impermeable area no greater than the permeable area: complies. Unlined over ground above 1×10⁻⁶ m/s: up to 5× the permeable area may be added (100 m² impermeable needs 20 m² permeable). Lined with added area: does not comply; add downstream interception.
ER-08.check: Lining, added area ratio and tested rate.
ER-08.note: This is a compliance presumption for the proposed feature, not a requirement to provide it. Apply the agreement and calculation conditions in ER-05 and national standards 2.6.2–2.7.

ER-09.title: Swales
ER-09.text: Fall under 1:100 with at least 500 mm suitable base: up to 5× the vegetated base area. Unlined, fall under 1:100 and over 1×10⁻⁶ m/s: up to 25×. Steeper than 1:100: no interception unless shown by design. Areas draining within 5 m of an unlined swale outlet do not count unless the swale is flat with a raised outlet.
ER-09.check: Long-section fall, base material, lining and outlet arrangement.
ER-09.note: This is a compliance presumption for the proposed feature, not a requirement to provide it. Apply the agreement and calculation conditions in ER-05 and national standards 2.6.2–2.7.

ER-10.title: Infiltration trenches and soakaways
ER-10.text: Roads drained by infiltration trenches comply. Areas drained to systems designed to infiltrate 1-in-1-month events comply.
ER-10.check: Design event for the infiltration system.
ER-10.note: This is a compliance presumption for the proposed feature, not a requirement to provide it. Apply the agreement and calculation conditions in ER-05 and national standards 2.6.2–2.7.

ER-11.title: Detention basins
ER-11.text: A flat, unlined vegetated basin base below the outlet, without specific provision routing low flows directly to the outlet, can receive up to five times that base area. Above 1×10⁻⁶ m/s infiltration, the ratio can be up to 25:1. Higher ratios need justification using below-outlet storage, higher infiltration rates and detailed design. Provide upstream sediment control for infiltrating basins.
ER-11.check: Effective below-outlet base area, lining, levels, low-flow routing, tested infiltration and sediment control; calculations for a higher ratio.
ER-11.note: This is a compliance presumption for the proposed feature, not a requirement to provide it. Apply the agreement and calculation conditions in ER-05 and national standards 2.6.2–2.7.

ER-12.title: Bioretention and rain gardens
ER-12.text: Unlined bioretention complies where the impermeable area is up to 5× the vegetated surface receiving runoff (100 m² needs 20 m²).
ER-12.when: Rain gardens, bioretention, tree pits designed as bioretention.
ER-12.note: This is a compliance presumption for the proposed feature, not a requirement to provide it. Apply the agreement and calculation conditions in ER-05 and national standards 2.6.2–2.7.

ER-13.title: Attenuation ponds give no interception
ER-13.text: Areas drained by attenuation ponds with a permanent pool are assumed not to deliver interception.
ER-13.note: This is a compliance presumption for the proposed feature, not a requirement to provide it. Apply the agreement and calculation conditions in ER-05 and national standards 2.6.2–2.7.

RV-01.title: Control rate and volume for the 1% and 50% events
RV-01.text: When discharging to a water body or sewer, control the 1% AEP runoff (rate and volume) so flood risk elsewhere does not increase, and the 50% AEP rate so it has no negative impact. Size infiltration for the design event.
RV-01.check: Event table showing 50%, 3.3% and 1% AEP rates.

RV-02.title: CDA: mimic greenfield, capped at the 1 in 10 year rate
RV-02.text: All off-site discharges should mimic greenfield performance up to a maximum of the 1 in 10 year greenfield rate. Where infiltration is not suitable, limit flows to the 1 in 10 year greenfield rate.
RV-02.when: Positive discharges subject to Torbay CDA criteria and applicable local planning policy.
RV-02.check: Event-specific greenfield performance and the Q10 ceiling; record the site and policy basis.

RV-03.title: 50% AEP limit
RV-03.text: Limit the 50% AEP peak to the 50% AEP greenfield rate (Qbar or Qmed) or 3 l/s/ha, whichever is greater.
RV-03.when: Discharge to surface waters or sewers.
RV-03.check: Qbar calculation and the allowable rate.

RV-04.title: 1% AEP limit: volume test
RV-04.text: Compare the volume discharged to surface waters or sewers in the developed 1% AEP 6-hour event with greenfield runoff volume for the same event. If greater, limit the 1% AEP peak to max(the 50% AEP greenfield rate, 3 l/s/ha). If equal or less, limit it to max(the 1% AEP greenfield rate, 3 l/s/ha). Distinguish runoff generated from the volume remaining to be discharged after interception, reuse or infiltration.
RV-04.when: Discharge to surface waters or sewers.
RV-04.check: The 6-hour discharged-volume comparison, its contributing area and the national branch used.

RV-05.title: Compare the applicable national and local limits
RV-05.text: Calculate the national 50% AEP limit and the correct 1% AEP volume branch. Separately show the applicable local greenfield performance and Q10 ceiling. Use the more stringent applicable criterion for each event where the evidence-based local approach satisfies national standard 3.10. Do not raise a calculated limit automatically to 1.5 l/s.
RV-05.when: Positive discharges where national and local criteria overlap.
RV-05.check: Use the runoff comparison; record the local policy basis, the governing event and any agreed departure.
RV-05.note: National 3.10 gives a more stringent, evidence-based local approach precedence. Torbay guide 3.5 says the CDA criteria take preference where they overlap. The CDA's 'mimic greenfield' has no 3 l/s/ha floor, so for small or low-runoff sites it is stricter than national 3.18.

RV-06.title: Check proposals relying on the published 1.5 l/s minimum
RV-06.text: The September 2022 Torbay guide states a minimum positive discharge of 1.5 l/s. Where that exceeds a current national or applicable local limit, record the conflict and obtain the approving body's agreement to the proposed approach.
RV-06.when: A proposal relies on 1.5 l/s despite a lower calculated limit.
RV-06.check: The lower calculated limit, evidence for the proposed control, blockage protection and the recorded approval or departure.
RV-06.note: This published local minimum is not a national exemption. It can conflict with low greenfield rates on sites of different sizes. The comparison tool leaves the conflict visible.

RV-07.title: Brownfield sites: check the greenfield expectation
RV-07.text: Torbay CDA advice and the published local guide expect brownfield runoff to meet greenfield criteria. National standard 3.21 permits an evidenced, agreed relaxation in defined circumstances, capped by 3.21.1. Do not assume that route overrides a more stringent applicable local approach.
RV-07.check: Greenfield rates used, not existing rates.
RV-07.note: National 3.21 allows a relaxation of up to 5× greenfield with evidence and agreement. The CDA and Torbay guide require brownfield to match greenfield, so assess whether the local approach takes precedence under national 3.10. Record the applicable geographic and policy basis and any requested departure.

RV-08.title: Tidal or sea outfalls
RV-08.text: Where runoff goes to a water body that can take uncontrolled discharge without environmental impact (the sea, large tidal estuaries), 3.3 and 3.4 may not apply, subject to written approval from the relevant risk management authority.
RV-08.when: Direct discharge to the sea or a large tidal estuary.
RV-08.check: Written approval; erosion, tide locking, water quality and ecology.

RV-09.title: Greenfield runoff method
RV-09.text: Estimate greenfield rates with the EA Flood Estimation Guidelines, using the whole area that could drain to the system (permeable and impermeable), with no climate change, and soil parameters confirmed by ground investigation.
RV-09.check: Method, area used, SOIL/HOST class evidence.

RV-10.title: Climate change: upper end allowance
RV-10.text: Use the latest EA allowances, upper end, for the epoch matching the design life. Torbay (South Devon catchment), 2070s epoch (2061 to 2125): +40% for 3.3% AEP and +50% for 1% AEP. 2050s epoch (2022 to 2060): +35% and +45%. Record the development's lifetime and how it is covered by the selected epoch.
RV-10.check: Allowance and epoch against the design life.
RV-10.note: National SuDS standard 3.8 specifies the upper-end allowance for drainage design. EA general surface-water FRA guidance separately describes central allowances for shorter lifetimes; do not substitute those for the national SuDS design requirement. The Torbay guide's 50% matches the 2070s upper end for the 1% event. For a shorter-lifetime proposal where the current national allowance is lower, record how the published local 50% criterion is applied and obtain agreement for the assessment basis.

RV-11.title: Urban creep: 10% on the proposed impermeable area
RV-11.text: Add 10% to the impermeable area of the proposed development in the calculations.
RV-11.note: National 3.33 applies 10% to impermeable area within property curtilages, and 0% for flats without private permeable space. Torbay's published expectation covers the whole proposed impermeable area. Show both scopes where they differ. Record the model areas, assessment basis and any council agreement; approval of a blanket reconciliation is not recorded.

RV-12.title: Latest rainfall data and runoff method
RV-12.text: Use the latest rainfall data (FEH22). Follow industry practice for runoff coefficients; do not ignore contributing pervious surfaces or SuDS footprints.

RV-13.title: Use the critical duration
RV-13.text: Use the critical duration storm to set maximum water levels, flows and storage. Different features may have different critical durations.

RV-14.title: Model the SuDS and pipes together
RV-14.text: Represent the SuDS features and the connecting pipe network as one model.
RV-14.check: One network model matching the layout drawings.

RV-15.title: Attenuate at several points
RV-15.text: Attenuate at multiple points across the development rather than one feature at the outfall, unless justified.

RV-16.title: Protect small flow controls
RV-16.text: Where the allowable rate needs an orifice (or equivalent) under 50 mm, protect it robustly from blockage. Assess blockage risk for all controls.

RV-17.title: Non-technical summary
RV-17.text: Provide detailed non-technical summaries of the design approach, calculations, results and conclusions.

FE-01.title: No flooding up to 3.3% AEP plus climate change
FE-01.text: No flooding on any part of the site up to the 3.3% AEP (1 in 30 year) event plus climate change, unless the area is designed to hold or convey water.
FE-01.check: Model results for the 3.3% AEP + cc event.

FE-02.title: Protect buildings, plant and escape routes up to 1% AEP plus climate change
FE-02.text: No flooding of buildings (including basements), utility plant susceptible to water, or safe access and escape routes up to the 1% AEP event plus climate change. Manage any system flooding within the development.
FE-02.check: Flood volumes and locations for 1% AEP + cc against levels.

FE-03.title: Below-ground storage: suggested modelling approaches
FE-03.text: Where there is no above-ground storage, Torbay suggests either: 1) 1% AEP + cc with top water level below the incoming pipe invert; or 2) 1% AEP with no flooding, and 3.3% AEP + cc top water level below the incoming pipe invert.
FE-03.check: Top water level against incoming invert.
FE-03.note: These are suggested modelling approaches. They do not replace the applicable national climate-adjusted performance, flooding and protected-receptor checks in FE-01 and FE-02.

FE-04.title: Provide freeboard
FE-04.text: Provide freeboard to buildings, vulnerable plant and escape routes, reflecting uncertainty and the consequence of flooding.

FE-05.title: Temporary flooding of shared spaces and roads
FE-05.text: Assess temporary flooding of multifunctional areas for risk, impact and recovery. Any flooding of highways shall be shallow, slow and low hazard and not affect escape routes.
FE-05.when: Designs that store water on open space or roads.

FE-06.title: Flows from adjacent land
FE-06.text: Account for runoff from adjacent sites onto the development. Convey it safely; no attenuation needed unless it interacts with the system. Off-site flooding up to 1% AEP should be managed or safely routed without increasing downstream risk.

FE-07.title: Surcharged outfalls and flood-locking
FE-07.text: Analyse the effect of a surcharged outfall and flood-locking (watercourse, sea, estuary or groundwater levels), adding storage if needed.
FE-07.when: Outfalls that may be submerged or surcharged.

FE-08.title: Keep features out of the 1% AEP flood area
FE-08.text: Do not place drainage features in areas at risk in the 1% AEP pluvial or fluvial event unless designed to operate in flood conditions.
FE-08.check: Feature locations against SFRA and EA mapping.

FE-09.title: Exceedance routes
FE-09.text: Assess events beyond 1% AEP and show exceedance routes on a plan, with no adverse risk to the development or elsewhere.

FE-10.title: Investigate blockage
FE-10.text: Investigate the effect of blockages on the system and show the resulting flood routes.
FE-10.check: Blockage scenario on the exceedance plan.

WQ-01.title: Base the treatment on a risk assessment
WQ-01.text: Base the management train on a water quality risk assessment matched to the pollution hazard and receiving water sensitivity. Use the Simple Index Approach (C753) or another agreed method.
WQ-01.check: Hazard level, sensitivity and treatment indices.

WQ-02.title: Provide a management train
WQ-02.text: Provide a management train using source, site and regional controls as needed.
WQ-02.check: Sequence of features on the layout.

WQ-03.title: Higher-risk land uses
WQ-03.text: Higher-risk uses may need proprietary treatment within the management train. Its evidence shall demonstrate necessary treatment throughout the development’s lifetime with appropriate maintenance. Very high-risk runoff requires discrete storage or treatment: where possible, discharge to a foul sewer under consent or use licensed off-site disposal. Environmental discharge is likely to require an EA permit.
WQ-03.when: Commercial yards, lorry parks, fuel or chemical handling, industrial sites.
WQ-03.check: Pollution hazard, lifetime treatment evidence, maintenance, discrete facilities where needed, sewer consent or disposal route and any permit.

WQ-04.title: Contain spills
WQ-04.text: As far as reasonably practicable, design for interception and containment of a pollution incident, removal of contaminated water and rehabilitation of the system. High-risk cases, such as discharge to a designated site, may need isolation controls.
WQ-04.when: All development; essential near designated sites.

WQ-05.title: Sediment remobilisation, climate resilience, amenity water
WQ-05.text: Mitigate sediment washout in higher flows. Keep features effective under climate change. Water in public view should be clear and free of odour, sheen and litter.

WQ-06.title: Treat harvested water for its use
WQ-06.text: Harvesting designs shall include the treatment needed for the intended use.

WQ-07.title: Standard 4 applies to sewer discharges
WQ-07.text: Standard 4 applies to discharges to surface water and combined sewers unless the sewerage undertaker sets stricter requirements.

WQ-08.title: Outfall hierarchy
WQ-08.text: Discharge to a water body should use, in order: an existing or new vegetated channel; reuse of an existing engineered outfall; a new engineered outfall designed for the watercourse hydromorphology.
WQ-08.when: Discharge to a watercourse or the sea.

WQ-09.title: Outfall covers and tracing
WQ-09.text: New outfalls should allow pollution tracing, with access covers showing water type and flow direction.

WQ-10.title: Pollution prevention plan near the SAC
WQ-10.text: Demolition or major development within 250 m of the Lyme Bay and Torbay SAC, or near a watercourse with a hydrological link to it, needs a pollution prevention plan by a suitably qualified person covering soil and sediment runoff.
WQ-10.when: Demolition or major development meeting the SAC trigger.

WQ-11.title: Local water improvement opportunities
WQ-11.text: Consider reasonable and practical opportunities to improve receiving waters or support nutrient neutrality, proportionate to the scale of the development. This is a requirement to consider opportunities; it does not require every proposal to deliver an improvement.
WQ-11.when: All applicable development, proportionate to scale.
WQ-11.check: Reference to the RBMP, DWMP or conservation objectives.

AB-01.title: Multifunctional design
AB-01.text: Adopt a SuDS approach that maximises amenity and demonstrates multifunctional water management. Keeping runoff at or near the surface is recommended. For surface features, high visual quality should have equal importance to functionality.
AB-01.check: Multifunctional design evidence, landscape integration and the reason for any below-ground solution.

AB-02.title: Follow local landscape guidance
AB-02.text: Select and design features with regard to topography, existing flow routes, geodiversity, character, habitats, cultural and historical associations, infiltration and discharge potential. Inform the design by relevant LPA landscape guidance, character assessments, green infrastructure strategies, design policies and codes.
AB-02.check: Site assessment and relevant Torbay landscape, green infrastructure and design documents.

AB-03.title: Planting, soils and biosecurity
AB-03.text: Where water is near the surface, vegetation and trees should be included as far as reasonably practicable. Species selection shall suit location, temperature, waterlogging and drought. Soil and aggregate specifications shall follow appropriate guidance. Planting operations shall comply with BS 3936-1:1992, BS 3936-10:1990 and BS 8545:2014, as specified in national footnote 32. Plant-selection guidance and sourcing that minimises biosecurity risks are recommendations.
AB-03.when: Vegetation or amenity features are proposed, with the recommendation to include vegetation applying where water is near the surface.
AB-03.check: Planting schedule, species tolerance, soil and aggregate specification and compliance with the planting standards in national footnote 32.

AB-04.title: Public appreciation and recreation
AB-04.text: Convey or attenuate runoff in features that maximise public appreciation. Where proposals form part of a streetscape or public space, include leisure and recreation where reasonably practicable.
AB-04.when: All applicable development; the recreation requirement applies to streetscapes and public spaces.

AB-05.title: Safety by design
AB-05.text: Apply good-practice principles to assess and manage risk in all cases. Shallow slopes, benching and margins are recommended for attenuation features. In community spaces, signage should explain function, public safety risks, benefits and authority contact details.
AB-05.when: All applicable development; apply the recommendations for attenuation features and community spaces where relevant.
AB-05.check: Risk assessment and management, safe access, depths, side slopes and edges; signage and interpretation where appropriate.

AB-06.title: Biodiversity risk and opportunity assessment at the outset
AB-06.text: Produce and agree a biodiversity risk and opportunity assessment at the start of design. It covers existing habitats and surveys, sensitivity, scale, local strategies (LNRS, RBMP) and BNG integration.
AB-06.when: All development, proportionate to scale and sensitivity.
AB-06.check: An agreed assessment at the outset: surveys and baseline habitats; site and wider catchment effects; hydrological changes affecting habitats; scale and sensitivity; local strategies; impacts, mitigation and opportunities; biodiversity net gain integration where applicable.

AB-07.title: Show the final design adds biodiversity value
AB-07.text: Provide evidence that the design follows the biodiversity mitigation hierarchy and relevant designated-site requirements, delivers resilient and self-sustaining habitats and corridors, supports connectivity, considers invasive species and integrates with standards 1–5. Where contributing to biodiversity net gain, local nature recovery or nutrient credits, demonstrate current best practice.
AB-07.check: Evidence addressing every item in national standard 6.7, including ecology and drainage interactions, wider-catchment impacts, habitat connectivity and the required mitigation.

CM-01.title: Management and maintenance plan
CM-01.text: Provide a management and maintenance plan that sustains performance against standards 1–6 for the development’s lifetime. Torbay asks for the plan and an inspection checklist. The detailed management and maintenance contents in national standards 7.10–7.11 are recommendations.
CM-01.when: All applicable development; establish the delivery arrangements at outline and supply detail appropriate to the application stage.
CM-01.check: Responsibilities and funding; asset and land ownership; easements; operating and pollution-incident instructions; establishment and routine maintenance; inspections, sediment and pollution controls and disposal; remedial work, replacement and post-flood rehabilitation.

CM-02.title: Consider failure scenarios
CM-02.text: Examine the likelihood and consequences of operational failure, including blocked structures and controls and failed pumps. Evaluate both flood risk and water quality impacts and manage the risks. The design should make consequential blockage or clogging apparent from surface inspection.
CM-02.check: Flood-risk and water-quality failure assessment, safe operation and the means of detecting failure.

CM-03.title: Access for maintenance
CM-03.text: Allow free, safe and easy access (with easements) for people, vehicles and machinery, including for emergencies.

CM-04.title: Sediment removal
CM-04.text: Design the system so sediment, detritus and debris can be easily removed. Easily emptied, replaced or rehabilitated sediment controls are recommended where deposits could harm performance or design life. Establish the lawful waste classification, handling and disposal route for removed material.
CM-04.check: Access, sediment controls, removal method, waste classification and the applicable disposal requirements.

CM-05.title: Automatic monitoring of pumps and proprietary products
CM-05.text: Where pumps or proprietary below-ground products (for example separators) are used, provide automatic monitoring and failure warnings to the responsible body.

CM-06.title: Performance monitoring
CM-06.text: Monitoring may be needed depending on scale and risk. Agree it with the approving body.

CM-07.title: Minimise energy and prioritise source control
CM-07.text: As far as reasonably practicable, minimise energy use over the design life. Prioritise source control to minimise large downstream attenuation ponds with safety-critical maintenance requirements.

CM-08.title: Ecology in maintenance
CM-08.text: Reference ecological surveys in maintenance planning. Consider invasive species and biosecurity in vegetation management.

CM-09.title: Construction information and phasing
CM-09.text: Give the contractor information on protecting and commissioning drainage during construction. For phased developments, provide a phased plan showing flow control in each phase.

CM-10.title: Build to the approved design
CM-10.text: Construct in strict accordance with the design. Report discrepancies to the designer and the council. The council may inspect and may take enforcement action.

CM-11.title: CDM and materials
CM-11.text: Designers take account of construction, operation, maintenance and decommissioning risks under CDM 2015 and minimise them as far as reasonably practicable. Specify materials suitable for their intended use, having regard to preserving natural resources and minimising embedded carbon.
CM-11.check: Designer’s risk assessment, operational access and suitable material specifications; no invented carbon threshold.

CM-12.title: Design life and loading
CM-12.text: Show components last the development's design life (or include replacement in the plan) and resist design loads with factors of safety. Underground storage must suit the final surface use.
CM-12.check: Product specifications; structural adequacy of crates under parking.

CM-13.title: No harm to nearby infrastructure
CM-13.text: Confirm construction and operation of SuDS do not harm nearby roads, railways or pipelines.

CM-14.title: Adoption routes
CM-14.text: Confirm who will own each asset. Sewers: South West Water under a section 104 agreement. Highway drainage: Torbay Highways under section 38, after the section 104 agreement. Other features: management company or owner. Planning approval does not mean the council adopts the system.
CM-14.check: Agreement in principle and a fallback if adoption is refused.

CM-15.title: Register of structures
CM-15.text: Following adoption, the local planning authority shall inform the lead local flood authority, which shall register the drainage system, including any non-adopted part. Record the adoption and notification arrangements.
CM-15.when: A drainage system has been adopted.
CM-15.check: Adoption record, LPA notification to the LLFA and registration covering the whole system.

SP-01.title: SuDS for all development that could affect drainage
SP-01.text: Development that could affect drainage on or around the site should include SuDS proportionate to its nature and scale, designed to the national standards, with acceptable operation for its lifetime. Major development takes account of LLFA advice.
SP-01.when: All development that could affect drainage, not only major.

SP-02.title: Statement of how the national standards are met
SP-02.text: Applications for development that could affect drainage should include a statement of how the national SuDS standards will be achieved.
SP-02.check: A statement covering all seven standards, proportionate to scale. The EA SuDS Strategy Templates give a ready format.

SP-03.title: Local Plan ER1 and ER2
SP-03.text: ER1: development safe for its lifetime, SuDS to restrict discharge rates, no increased discharge from Ilsham CSO, contributions where needed. ER2: water efficiency, protection of waters, pollution prevention plans, separate foul and surface water, and the drainage hierarchy.
SP-03.check: Policy compliance in the planning assessment.

SP-04.title: Torbay submission list
SP-04.text: Expect: percolation tests and geotechnical report; one hydraulic model of SuDS and pipes; layout drawings (cover and invert levels, pipe sizes, lengths, gradients, gullies, numbering, catchments); flow control details; SuDS details; construction drawings; maintenance plan and inspection checklist; exceedance and blockage plan; connection permissions; evidence the hierarchy was followed.

SP-05.title: Proportionate evidence by stage
SP-05.text: Outline: feasible strategy, space and levels, destination evidence, indicative storage. Full and reserved matters: complete detailed design. Conditions: exactly what the condition asks for.
SP-05.check: That missing detail is appropriate to the stage, not deferred without a feasible strategy.

SP-06.title: Recommend the national SuDS Strategy Template
SP-06.text: The EA templates (major and non-major) set out per-standard questions and evidence boxes. Completed templates make checking faster.
SP-06.check: Template sections against the evidence submitted.

SP-07.title: LLFA role
SP-07.text: Torbay is the Lead Local Flood Authority and statutory consultee for major development surface water drainage. For non-major development, the planning officer applies NPPF F8 and the Validation List with drainage advice as needed.

SP-08.title: Other consents are separate
SP-08.text: Planning permission does not replace ordinary watercourse consent (Torbay, Land Drainage Act), EA flood risk activity permits, sewer connection approval, highway approval, environmental permits or landowner consent.
SP-08.when: Schemes affecting watercourses, sewers or highways.

SP-09.title: Non-mains foul drainage assessment
SP-09.text: Development using non-mains foul drainage needs a foul drainage assessment justifying why mains connection is not feasible.

SP-10.title: Departures
SP-10.text: A national “shall” requirement needs an agreed departure to vary it; a “should” recommendation needs appropriate justification for an alternative. Where constraints prevent full compliance, maximise delivery and develop the justification in consultation with the approving body. A departure cannot override a prohibiting regulatory control. “Must” denotes a legislative or statutory obligation.
SP-10.check: The precise requirement, constraints, maximised delivery, reason, agreement and any overriding regulatory control.

SEALINK.title: Sea Link, Document 9.17.2: Kent Drainage Strategy, Version B
SEALINK.status: PINS EN020026-002822. Published applicant examination evidence; not a Torbay standard or an approved model design.

BLACKS.title: Blacks Head Inn drainage strategy, Issue 3, December 2025
BLACKS.publisher: Cole Easdon; Cherwell Council planning register
BLACKS.status: Published applicant evidence for 25/03340/F. Permitted on 30 September 2026, subject to conditions; condition 2 includes Drainage Strategy Issue 3. This does not establish Torbay compliance or an approved model for other sites.

MILLHOLME.title: Millholme Farm FRA and drainage strategy, 26014-01 Revision A
MILLHOLME.publisher: Coast Consulting Engineers; Redcar and Cleveland planning register
MILLHOLME.status: Published single-dwelling applicant evidence for R/2026/0284/FF. The inspected record showed no decision; use with the successive LLFA reviews, not as a compliant model.

NAT.status: Current. Non-statutory. NPPF F8.2 says SuDS should be designed in accordance with them.

EATPL.publisher: Environment Agency with CIRIA, ASA and Arup

C753.status: Industry guidance cited by the national standards. Access through CIRIA, subject to membership entitlement and current terms.
